create.name: Crazyhouse Xiangqi: a sample game, annotated
create.description: Fairy-Stockfish against itself under the site rules, five seconds a move, read again by Fairy-Stockfish. From the Crazyhouse Xiangqi rules page at mistboard.com/rules/crazyhouse-xiangqi.

chapter.name: A comeback, and a soldier drop mates

annotations.text: P@e9: a soldier dropped beside the general. The chariot on e8 guards it, and Black’s own horse blocks f10. Mate.

comments.text: d4-e3: an advisor takes the cannon that gave check.
N@f8+: the first of four drops in a row, each with check: horse, soldier, cannon, horse.
e3-d4: the advisor steps out of the palace to take back on d4.
The horse steps back to c8, and Red is winning from here.
Black drops a soldier on d5, and its chances fall from four in ten to one in four. The engine would first drop an elephant on d7 to cover the palace.
N@e9: Black spends the horse it just won on defence, and Red is clearly better.
f5-e7: the horse takes the middle soldier, and the game turns. Red is ahead for the rest of the game.
d5-g5: Black's cannon wins a soldier.
Red drops the chariot it has just won back on f1, and Black takes over. The engine would drop an elephant there and keep the chariot in hand.
f1-f10+: the chariots trade on Black’s back rank, and Red drops its new one on f1 at once.
A@e3, then A@d4 two moves later: one advisor at the top of the palace, one in front of it.

Fairy-Stockfish against itself at five seconds a move, read again by Fairy-Stockfish at four seconds a position. Red falls behind when it drops its chariot straight back on f1, and stays behind until the horse takes the middle soldier on move 21. Black's soldier drop on d5 on move 25 is the move that loses.
